inline_comments.comment: This filter silently removes valid pie sections with less than 1% of the total value. This is not related to the stated fix (negative/zero values) and introduces a silent data-loss regression. For example, a chart with 101 equal-value sections would have every section at ~0.99%, and ALL sections would be filtered — leaving an empty pie circle with all labels still in the legend. The behavior is undocumented, there is no warning to the user, and the 1% threshold is arbitrary. If the intent is to avoid rendering imperceptibly thin slices, this should at minimum warn the user (e.g., via a log message) or be documented. Consider removing this filter entirely since the DB-layer validation in `addSection` already prevents 0 and negative values from causing the original crash.

`filteredArcs` is always identical to `arcs` and this filter is dead code. `createPieArcs` already filters out any section with `(value / sum) * 100 < 1`, meaning every arc in `arcs` has at least 1% of the total. Consequently, `((datum.data.value / sum) * 100).toFixed(0)` for any arc in `arcs` will never equal `'0'` — it is always at least `'1'`. The comment `// Filter out arcs that would render as 0%` is misleading because this case cannot arise. Remove `filteredArcs` and use `arcs` directly, or consolidate the filtering logic in a single place.

`sum` is computed redundantly: once inside `createPieArcs` (via `reduce`) and again here in `draw` (via `forEach`). Both iterate over the same `sections` from `db.getSections()`. Consider returning the sum alongside the arcs from `createPieArcs`, or computing it once and passing it down, to avoid the double iteration.

`pieData` is pre-sorted descending (line 18) and then passed to `d3pie()`, which by default also sorts descending. The pre-sort is therefore redundant with d3's internal sort. The original code had this same double-sort. The clean fix would be to either (a) drop the pre-sort and rely solely on d3's default sort, or (b) keep the pre-sort and call `.sort(null)` on the `d3pie` instance to disable d3's internal sort (making the order explicitly deterministic). The current form is correct but unnecessarily redundant.

A test with the identical description `'should handle simple pie with zero slice value'` already exists in the base codebase (asserting that zero is accepted and stored). This PR replaces that test body with one that expects a rejection, but both tests have the same name within the same `describe` block. Duplicate test names cause ambiguity in test reports and can mask failures depending on the test runner. The old test should be explicitly removed or renamed in this diff to make the intent clear and avoid confusion.

There is already a test `'should handle simple pie with negative decimal'` in the base codebase (lines 133–140) that tests the same negative-value scenario but only asserts `.rejects.toThrowError()` without checking the error message. This PR adds a second, more specific negative-value test. The older generic test is now effectively superseded but was not removed, leaving redundant test coverage. Consider replacing or removing the older test to keep the test suite clean.

The test description `'should render pie slices only for non-zero values but shows all legends'` is inaccurate. None of the values in the test data (`386`, `85`, `1`) are zero. `'Rats': 1` is filtered because it represents 0.21% of the total (below the 1% threshold in `createPieArcs`), not because it is zero. A more accurate description would be something like `'should omit slices for sections below 1% of total but still show them in the legend'`. This aligns the test intent with the actual behavior under test.

`darshan.html` appears to be a personal developer test page named after the author. Personal sandbox files like this should not be committed to the shared repository. If a reproducible manual test case is needed, it should use a generic name (e.g., `pie-negative-values.html`) consistent with the project's naming conventions and placed in a location where such test pages are maintained.
There is an extra space in `FLOAT_PIE |  INT_PIE` (two spaces before `INT_PIE`). Should be `FLOAT_PIE | INT_PIE` for consistency with the rest of the grammar file.

The file is missing a newline at the end (the diff footer shows `\ No newline at end of file`). Most editors and linters expect a trailing newline in text files, and its absence can cause noisy diffs in future changes.

The error message ends with a period: `All slice values must be > 0.` The two new unit tests use `.toThrowError(substring)` which performs a substring match, so the trailing period is not asserted. This means the period (or any other tail characters after `> 0`) could silently change in the future without the tests catching it. Consider using `.toThrowError(/exact regex/)` or `.toThrowError(new Error(...))` in the tests for a more precise assertion, or at least document that substring matching is intentional.

general_comments.comment: The PR conflates two distinct concerns: (1) preventing crashes from negative/zero values (addressed via grammar + DB-layer validation), and (2) silently suppressing small-value slices (< 1% filter in `createPieArcs`). The title and description only mention the first concern, but the renderer changes introduce the second as an undocumented side-effect. This separation of concerns should be made explicit: either scope the PR to just the validation fix and leave the small-value rendering as a follow-up, or explicitly document the 1% filtering behavior in the PR description and in user-facing docs.

The `< 1%` filter in `createPieArcs` is unsafe for datasets with many sections. If a pie chart has more than 100 equal-value sections, each section would be below 1% and every section would be filtered out, resulting in a completely empty pie chart with all items visible only in the legend. There is no user feedback (no error, no log warning) to explain what happened. Since the DB-layer validation in `addSection` already rejects zero and negative values — preventing the original crash — this filter provides no crash-prevention benefit and only introduces data-accuracy risk.

The changeset description (`Prevents crashes during parsing by validating values post-parsing`) is self-contradictory: crashes during parsing are prevented by the grammar change (accepting negatives), not by post-parsing validation. The post-parsing validation in `addSection` provides better error messages. The changeset would be clearer as: `Fix parser crash on negative values by accepting them in the grammar and rejecting them in the DB layer with a user-friendly error message.`
